시편-58-1.title: 시편 58장 1절 역사문법적 주해
시편-58-1.exegesis: 9-10. As His mercy and truth, so shall His praise, fill the universe.
시편-58-1.theologicalNote: 9-10. As His mercy and truth, so shall His praise, fill the universe.

시편-58-2.title: 시편 58장 2절 역사문법적 주해
시편-58-2.exegesis: PSALM 58 Psa 58:1-11 . David's critical condition in some period of the Sauline persecution probably occasioned this Psalm, in which the Psalmist teaches that the innate and actual sinfulness of men deserves, and shall receive, God's righteous vengeance, while the pious may be consoled by the evidence of His wise and holy government of men. 1. O congregation-- literally, "Oh, dumb"; the word used is never translated "congregation." "Are ye dumb? ye should speak righteousness," may be the translation. In any case, the writer remonstrates with them, perhaps a council, who were assembled to try his cause, and bound to give a right decision.

시편-58-3.exegesis: 2. This they did not design; but weigh ... violence-- or give decisions of violence. Weigh is a figure to express the acts of judges. in the earth-- publicly.

시편-58-8.title: 시편 58장 8절 역사문법적 주해
시편-58-8.exegesis: 7. which run continually-- literally, "they shall go to themselves," utterly depart, as rapid mountain torrents. he bendeth ... his arrows-- prepares it. The term for preparing a bow applied to arrows ( Psa 64:3 ). let them ... pieces-- literally, "as if they cut themselves off"--that is, become blunted and of no avail.

시편-58-11.title: 시편 58장 11절 역사문법적 주해
시편-58-11.exegesis: 10-11. wash ... wicked-- denoting great slaughter. The joy of triumph over the destruction of the wicked is because they are God's enemies, and their overthrow shows that He reigneth (compare Psa 52:5-7; 54: 7 ). In this assurance let heaven and earth rejoice ( Psa 96:10 ; 97:1 , &c.).
